claims.text: The applicable alloy system is CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed intervention is a neural-network potential trained on a large dataset of ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations of the liquid phase.
Training-data quality, training-data diversity, and regularization can prevent or mitigate overfitting.
The proposed NNP can improve representation of liquid CoCrFeMnNi relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The NNP can capture complex many-body interactions and accommodate diverse atomic configurations in the liquid.
Incorporating ab initio liquid configurations into the reference potential will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Reduced thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will produce more accurate thermodynamic-property predictions.
The proposed temperature range is 1500–2000 K.
The range 1500–2000 K is near and above the melting point of CoCrFeMnNi.
Entropy, enthalpy, and free energy will be compared between calculations using the NNP and TOR-TILD EAM references.
Failure of the NNP to produce a significant reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch would falsify the hypothesis.
